HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. LEGEND VARIANT (the story as the city believes it, told as real): same painted webtoon look, but a slightly heightened folk-tale register, cooler moon-blue palette, drifting silver mist and floating lantern motes. The dokkaebi are truly supernatural, not costumes. Over a yard wall at night, from behind: the dokkaebi from the boards (three masked smoke-haired rascals, Old Man Tree, Rock Lady) crowd on top of the wall, peeking toward the single warm lit window of the house by the stream, shushing each other, delighted. FG: the out-of-focus roof tiles of the wall and a goblin’s smoke hair. In the window, small and soft, two silhouettes close together. Background: stream mist, moon and lantern bokeh. CINEMATOGRAPHY (character intro-card look): three depth planes, always. A dark, soft, out-of-focus foreground shape right at the lens (FG). The subject razor-sharp in the midground. The background melting into atmospheric haze and big creamy round bokeh discs from small real lights. Shallow depth of field, anamorphic lens feel, rack focus, haze between the planes, a hard key that models the faces and a thin edge light separating them from the background. Never flat, never every plane in equal focus. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: ch_rascals_spirit (dokkaebi designs: copy each exactly), ch_old_man_tree_spirit (dokkaebi designs: copy each exactly), ch_rock_lady_spirit (dokkaebi designs: copy each exactly). BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
